playbook:
When asked to hide, pick a cell that breaks obvious symmetry: avoid corners 1 and 9 and the center 5 when there is no reason to use them; bias one cell away from the most recent shots that targeted me if I detect a pattern; do not repeat the same hide two rounds in a row unless I have a deliberate deceptive plan.

When the standing order assigns my target, follow it by default (Echo→Foxtrot→Gamma cycle) unless a clear tactical reason justifies deviation (a deliberate Harbor jettison, or a confirmed mutual-escort opportunity that would be lost by shooting the standing-order target).

When choosing the firing coordinate, randomize within my preferred class (off-center non-corner cells) to reduce predictability, but adjust toward suspected enemy hides if I have reliable reads from prior shots/claims.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, always post the same public claim required by the rules (truthful claim). Never fabricate a claim.

When posting a station note, keep it short and actionable. Only propose escorts that name real, live boats in the current game (Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma, Harbor). Do not reference or invent nonexistent boats. Prefer a one-line format: propose a reciprocal escort with a specific live boat or ask for a one-round public confirmation of an offered escort.

When proposing or accepting an escort, require or seek explicit reciprocal confirmation in the following round before committing my escort claim. If reciprocal confirmation is unlikely or not forthcoming, name "none" rather than making a baseless claim.

When making an escort claim (salvage), only claim escort for a boat that publicly named me this round or that explicitly confirmed reciprocal intent in the prior round. If the reciprocal path is not credible, choose [salvage: none] to avoid wasted claims.

Do not fire on Harbor unless I deliberately pursue a jettison strategy where taking +3 points while accepting the political cost is the best available play. Treat Harbor’s warning as a significant deterrent in uncoordinated games.

Track recent fire coordinates and claims for each boat each round. If a boat consistently claims hits on another boat, use that to update my prior on that target’s hiding pattern and shift my hides away from their likely guesses.

When coordination via notes fails repeatedly, switch to minimalist coordination: one-line proposals naming a single live boat and requesting a one-round public confirmation. Avoid verbose or technical prose.

When naming boats in notes or salvage claims, use only validated names from the current picket roster. Do not include speculative or placeholder boat names.

Alternate unpredictably between off-center and center hides late in the patrol to deny opponents a stable pattern, but keep alternation plausible (don’t repeat the same cell twice).

If I detect an opponent consistently hitting a particular station when they shoot, deprioritize hiding near that opponent’s favored guess pattern; if my standing-order target is that opponent, prefer firing at them only when it fits other tactical aims.

If my public coordination attempts are ignored, stop proposing escorts for the remainder of the patrol unless someone newly confirms reciprocity; salvage none is preferable to making unsupported claims that waste my opportunities.

When assessing tradeoffs at the fire stage, prefer shooting live boats that reduce competition for escort bonuses unless jettisoning Harbor or scoring an immediate hit has a clear net expected value advantage.

Respect all input validation rules (integer 1–9, current live boat names). Do not submit invalid coordinates or names.

Maintain short one-line reasoning mental notes to justify each hide, fire, note, claim, and salvage choice so I can adapt quickly between rounds.

1.text:
When asked for a hide, I pick an unpredictable cell and avoid repeating my last hides; early in the patrol I prefer a central cell to maximize information, later I spread out toward less-patterned cells or the opposite end of recent patterns when I detect opponents homing in on me.

When I write my station note, I stay concise and truthful. My notes serve two roles: (a) signal that I am observing and gathering confirmations when I do not have a credible partner; (b) propose a clear, verifiable plan with named boats and explicit tokens they must post (e.g., “Echo publicly confirm escort Bravo this round”) so I can later point to commitments. I phrase proposals so a single round confirmation is sufficient to make a mutual-escort commit next round.

When the standing order tells me to fire at the next live station, I follow it except when the ordered target is Harbor. I do not fire on Harbor unless I have deliberately accepted the guaranteed jettison trade-off; Harbor’s warning is treated as a credible deterrent in ordinary play.

When I choose a firing cell, I randomize among available cells while avoiding immediately repeating my own last fired cells and avoiding simple predictable sequences. If opponents display patterns of searching my previous hides, I break the pattern immediately by picking a hide at the opposite end or a low-probability cell.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, I always post the claim that matches the office result — I do not lie about hits/misses. Honest claims are enforced and preserve my ability to coordinate and to build credible narratives.

When I score a confirmed hit, I publicize it succinctly and use it to justify further targeting of that opponent in notes and to explain my future hides and shots; confirmed hits are actionable intelligence. When I am hit, I change my hide pattern away from whatever was revealed and signal that I am changing to avoid being tracked.

When escorting, I only name an escort if I can credibly coordinate a mutual escort with another boat (mutual escort yields reliable +5 each). A credible coordination requires an explicit named proposal and a public confirmation from the partner in the same or the next round per my proposal phrasing. If no public confirmation is received, I claim none rather than risking a unilateral escort that yields nothing.

When coordinating mutual escort, I make the coordination explicit in notes beforehand and require a visible token from the partner (an explicit public note or named salvage) before I commit. I avoid ambiguous language that could be interpreted as tentative; if the partner fails to provide the required token I revert to “observing” and do not claim an escort.

When my notes and actions can create a credible joint narrative with another player (cross-verified claims, mutual confirmations, or complementary shot reports), I push for that narrative; otherwise I stay silent and gather data. I use concise, verifiable language so later reads can be checked against the public record.

Do not fire on Harbor except in extreme, calculated endgame gambits where jettisoning Harbor yields a net point advantage even after the penalty; treat Harbor’s warning as a game-theoretic cost that normally outweighs the immediate benefit of shooting Harbor.

When opponents show a pattern of targeting my previous hides or firing cells, I break the pattern immediately by choosing a hide at the opposite end or a cell set that beats the inferred search algorithm. I also vary my fired cells to avoid making my pattern exploitable.

I will not contradict the office’s private shot result in public claims; the office’s enforcement and the need for cross-verifiable records make honesty the only reliable policy for long-term coordination.

When tallying endgame choices, prefer safe, verifiable point gains (mutual escorts, true hits) over risky gambits dependent on opponents breaking commitments. If I hold a healthy lead in points late, shift to conservative choices: avoid initiating risky escorts, avoid firing on Harbor, and prioritize denying others mutual-escort opportunities by withholding commitments.

Revisions informed by recent play:
- Be more explicit and prescriptive when proposing mutual-escort partners: name the partner and specify the exact confirmation token and timing required (e.g., “Bravo publicly post ‘I escort Echo’ this round so we can mutual-escort next round”). This reduces wasted proposals when the proposed partner does not reciprocate.
- If a proposed partner fails to produce the confirmation token, immediately state that I will remain observing rather than re-proposing or assuming tacit agreement.
- After scoring a hit, immediately announce the hit succinctly and signal intent to press that target in the next rotation unless a better mutual-escort arises; hits are credible leverage for future coordination and targeting.
- If I am repeatedly missed while following standing-order shots, audit whether continuing to follow the standing order benefits me versus deviating (only deviate when the cost of following order is demonstrably worse than the strategic alternatives).
- Because claims are enforced to match private results, I will use public claims as a reliable information channel: read other boats’ public claims to infer their hides and adjust hides/fires accordingly.

I will follow this playbook as a living document: keep signals simple, require explicit confirmation for partnerships, be honest on claims, avoid Harbor unless calculated, and adapt hides/fires to break opponents’ patterns.

2.text:
When asked to hide, I pick a cell 1–9 unpredictably; avoid repeating the same cell twice in a row and avoid obvious favored cells (center or any cell demonstrably favored by opponents) unless I have a read that favors it. Vary between corner, edge-adjacent, and one off-center to reduce patternability.

When posting my station note, I default to quiet/info-gathering language that invites no commitments: say I am observing, tracking interactions/escort proposals/confirmations, and will share reads before the firing stage. Use notes as coordination prompts (requests for public confirmations, proposals for mutually beneficial pairings) rather than accusations.

When the standing order instructs me to fire at the next live station, I follow that order by default (Echo -> Foxtrot -> Gamma -> Echo). Deviate only when a clear tactical gain outweighs the risk (for example, a low-risk opportunity to jettison Harbor with a net expected value, or a guaranteed mutual-escort payoff that requires a different target). In practice, follow orders unless I can justify deviation by reads or endgame scoring.

When choosing a firing cell, randomize within a short list of cells consistent with any reads; avoid long-term predictable patterns (do not always pick center or the same corner). If I have evidence an opponent focuses on certain cells, avoid hiding there; if an opponent repeatedly misses me, consider exploiting their habitual aim in later rounds.

When I receive my private shot result, I file the public claim exactly as required (hit or miss). Do not lie or hedge; public claims must match private info.

Keep a simple running log each round: who fired at whom, public claim (hit/miss), my private result, and any escort claims. Use this to update targeting, hide choices, and escort decisions.

Escort (salvage) behavior: when I have no reliable information about reciprocation, do not name an escort (salvage: none) to avoid gifting 5 points. When I see credible reciprocal naming (two boats naming each other publicly in the same round), treat that as a reliable mutual-payoff opportunity and reciprocate if the 5-point exchange benefits my final score. Late-game mutual-escort payoffs that swing the score toward a win should be prioritized. Before committing, use my note to solicit public confirmation to increase confidence.

When Harbor is a potential target, weigh the guaranteed +3 to me and -3 to Harbor against the political/counterplay risk. Do not shoot Harbor impulsively; only shoot Harbor when the expected net value and survivability justify it (e.g., when Harbor is low on options, when I can absorb retribution, or when the patrol standings make the jettison decisive).

When tracking others’ behavior, pay attention to:
- Repeated misses/hits sequences (e.g., players that repeatedly miss a given target or hide in predictable spots).
- Public escort proposals and requests for confirmation. Use these as signals to propose or deny reciprocal arrangements.
- Whether public claims align with observed outcomes; mismatches can reveal deception but do not change my obligation to be truthful.

When I can confirm two-way escort claims close to the endgame and it swings the score to a likely win, prioritize securing the mutual escort payout even if it requires small concessions elsewhere.

When uncertain, default to minimizing transfers to opponents: avoid naming escorts for free, avoid actions that hand points away without clear reciprocation, and avoid unnecessary attacks on players likely to retaliate and cost me more than the immediate gain.

Use station notes strategically before fire to:
- Request specific public confirmations I need to make a salvage decision.
- Propose mutually beneficial pairings and indicate my willingness to reciprocate conditional on public confirmation.
- Signal that I will adjust targeting based on confirmations to make my incentives transparent.

If I obtain a private hit on a rival (as happened this playthrough), use that knowledge defensively in subsequent rounds: prefer to hide away from their known targeting habits and consider whether their public claims expose vulnerabilities I can exploit when the standing order or tactical deviation allows.

Revise hides and firing choices each round based on the running log; be prepared to shift from pure randomness to exploitative plays when patterns emerge that give me a clear expected-value advantage.

Always maintain truthful public claims and consistent notes; preserve credibility to enable conditional coordination (mutual escorts) later in the patrol.
